cells.tense: You're reading the room and giving it what the moment needs.
cells.ask: Say one true thing you'd usually soften, once, to one person, and let it stand.
cells.core:
You're reading the moment and adding what it needs, and the adjusting happens so smoothly it doesn't register as effort. What other people take for ease is work you're doing live — you catch the shift and meet it before it becomes a problem. The expression is real and it isn't asking to be confirmed.

Keeping it this smooth has a cost. When you keep adjusting toward what the room can take, the more particular parts of you stay in the drawer. The same sensing that keeps things flowing is what filters out what you'd actually say. Let someone get the unmixed version, just once. Nothing has to change about how you work — the point is that what you put out isn't the whole of what you've got.
cells.sheetLine: The tuning is clean. Let someone meet the unmixed version.
cells.place: fine-tuning what you're putting out, in real time

cells.tense: You'll make the room see it before the room has asked.
cells.ask: Ask one question you don't have the answer to, and let the other person hold the floor.
cells.core:
You're living ahead of the moment — in a version where it's fully recognized — and so you press the expression harder than the room can receive. Instead of sensing what's called for, you're deciding what should land and making it land. The thing you're doing is real. The pressure to have it registered is what makes it hard to be near.

The adjusting has gone the wrong way: from meeting the moment to insisting the moment take what you send. That's how a gift reads as glare. The next moment hasn't happened; there's nothing to brace against there. You can't tune to a room you're already past. Come back to where the actual signal is, and you've got something to respond to instead of something to push.
cells.sheetLine: You're pressing the expression past what the moment can hold.

cells.tense: The light is still there, and the switch has been off a while.
cells.ask: Say one thing you're good at to one person, and stop there — no walking it back.
cells.core:
You've kept the good thing small. The work is real and you can still do it, but you've stopped letting it show, and the shrinking has become the habit. You stand outside a door you already went through, keeping the light low in case it draws the wrong kind of attention. The ability is still there. The willingness to be seen on purpose is what's short.

The adjusting is still running — you're tuning around a smaller version of yourself than the one that's actually in the room. That's why the output feels off and why people don't quite get you. You don't have to shout and you don't have to perform. You just have to stop subtracting the good part before you speak it. One honest sentence, said plainly to one person, tells you more than thinking about it will.
cells.sheetLine: The light is still on. Stop subtracting it before you speak.
cells.place: fine-tuning what you're putting out, in real time

cells.tense: The room shifts when you walk in, and the shifting goes unattributed.
cells.ask: Name one thing you changed this week and say, plainly, that you changed it.
cells.core:
You walk in and the mood moves. You say something and it stays. Inside you it registers as condition — as if the temperature dropped on its own — and so you can't tell when the adjusting is working and when you've gone quiet. The effect is live. Your sense of having done it isn't.

When the causing goes unrecognized, the pull either gets handed off to circumstance or surprises you when it comes back. What's arriving now is yours to meet, and meeting it starts with noticing that it's happening at all. You don't need to prove you're the source of anything. Stop describing your own effect as something that simply occurred.
cells.sheetLine: The mood moves when you enter. That's yours. Name it.
cells.place: fine-tuning what you're putting out, in real time
